title: Prescriptive JSON format and unified error taxonomy for tool parameter coercion
creator: Ariana Kapoor
description: Background: We need a deterministic, prescriptive JSON definition format and runtime policy for tool/function calling parameters that reduces ambiguous coercion behavior across SDKs and the runtime. Current issues include: inconsistent coercion between SDKs, poor human-readable errors, and lack of telemetry for common conversion failures. Goal: Define a single canonical JSON 'ParamManifest' format, three supported coercion modes (strict, permissive, repair), a unified error taxonomy with stable error codes, and a compatibility layer for legacy parameter shapes. This ticket captures the spec, runtime contract, migration guidance, and acceptance criteria for implementing the first pass in the runtime and Python/TS SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: A minimal ParamManifest JSON schema is documented and checked into docs (README + Console UX example).
Runtime supports coercion modes: strict (reject on mismatch), permissive (best-effort coercion w/warnings), repair (attempt transformations and return structured repair hints).
Errors emitted follow the unified taxonomy and include stable codes (eg. TP-001..TP-010), remediation hints, and a 'suggestedFix' field when available.
SDKs (python + ts) implement client-side validation that mirrors runtime behavior and surface identical error codes/messages.
Telemetry events emitted for validation failures include: error_code, field_path, coercion_mode, attempted_transformations, and request_id.
A compatibility shim for legacy aliases (param name aliases and simple shape upgrades) is implemented behind a flag and documented for customers.
Integration tests cover: schema mismatch, missing required field, array->single coercion, numeric-string conversion, and repair suggestion flow.
implementation_plan: Draft ParamManifest v0 with examples for primitives, arrays, enums, object shapes, and 'oneOf' preference ordering.
Define coercion modes semantics and a canonical priority list for transforms (e.g., string->number only in permissive/repair; number->string always allowed).
Design unified error taxonomy and stable codes (TP-001..TP-020) and map to HTTP/SDK exceptions.
Add telemetry hooks in runtime to emit validation events and surface aggregated dashboards in Console (validation type, freq, top fields).
Implement runtime validator library (golang/ts bridge) that exposes a concise API for callers and returns structured error objects (used by runtime & SDKs).
Update python/ts SDKs to run the same validator locally when user passes ParamManifest; ensure identical messages and codes.
Create migration doc and a console toggle for enabling legacy alias compat shim per model/route.
Ship feature behind feature-flag and run canary on internal customers and a sample partner integration.
migration_strategy: Stage 1: Publish ParamManifest docs and opt-in SDK validators (no default change). Stage 2: Enable telemetry for manifest mismatches and collect a 2-week baseline. Stage 3: Roll out permissive coercion as default for legacy routes while blocking strict mode for new APIs. Stage 4: After 6 weeks of telemetry and customer opt-ins, flip default to strict for new public endpoints and offer repair suggestions for legacy routes.
proposed_error_codes: TP-001: missing_required - Required field is absent. message: 'Missing required parameter {field_path}'.
TP-002: type_mismatch - Value has wrong type; includes expectedType and actualType.
TP-003: enum_violation - Value not in allowed enumerated set; includes allowedValues list.
TP-004: coercion_failed - Runtime attempted coercion but could not convert (shows attemptedTransforms).
TP-005: array_cardinality - Array cardinality mismatch (expected single vs array).
TP-006: unknown_field - Received field not present in ParamManifest (suggest nearestName if available).
TP-007: numeric_overflow - Numeric conversion would overflow configured bounds.
TP-008: json_parse_error - Parameter value failed JSON parse for typed string input.
TP-009: repair_suggested - Validator created a candidate repair and includes 'suggestedFix' and 'confidence'.
TP-010: compatibility_alias_applied - A legacy alias mapping was applied; emitted at 'info' level.
sample_error_payloads: {"error_code": "TP-001", "message": "Missing required parameter 'address.street'", "field_path": "address.street", "remediation": "Provide 'address.street' as a string. Example: {\"address\": {\"street\": \"123 Main St\"}}"}

{"error_code": "TP-002", "message": "Type mismatch for 'timeoutMs' (expected integer, got string)", "field_path": "timeoutMs", "expectedType": "integer", "actualType": "string", "remediation": "Pass timeoutMs as a number or enable permissive mode to auto-coerce."}

{"error_code": "TP-004", "message": "Coercion failed for 'items.price'", "field_path": "items[2].price", "attemptedTransforms": ["string->number", "trim-whitespace"], "remediation": "Ensure numeric string is well-formed (e.g., '12.50')."}

{"error_code": "TP-009", "message": "Repair suggested for 'user.email'", "field_path": "user.email", "suggestedFix": "trim and lower-case value", "confidence": "0.85", "remediation": "Review suggestedFix and call /validate?applyRepair=true to auto-apply."}
telemetry_events: validation.failure - emitted when a TP-* error occurs: {error_code, field_path, coercion_mode, request_id, route, model, sdk_version}
validation.repair_applied - emitted when repair mode applies a candidate: {field_path, transform_list, confidence, request_id}
validation.alias_resolution - emitted when a legacy alias is used: {alias, canonical_name, request_id}
validation.metrics.snapshot - periodic aggregate: {route, errors_by_code, pct_requests_with_validation, avg_repairs_per_request}
open_questions: Should repair mode be allowed by default for Hosted API or restricted to Dedicated/Private initially?
What SLA impact do we accept for permissive coercion on latency-sensitive endpoints? We should quantify p50/p95 overhead.
Do we expose 'suggestedFix' auto-apply via an optional query param (/validate?applyRepair=true) or via a separate repair API?
What is the long-term plan for error code namespace? (TP- vs VLD-).
How to represent deeply nested field paths consistently across languages (dot vs bracket notation) — pick one canonical format.

notes: Avoid auto-trimming that would change user intent for free-text fields (eg. 'bio'). Coercion rules should be conservative by default; repairs should be explicit and surfaced in audit logs for Private customers.
